B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: COROS states that COROS MCP itself is free. The AI platform may charge separately or impose subscription and usage limits.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: COROS account required; no MCP-specific COROS subscription price is stated. Some AI platforms may require a paid plan for connectors or MCP access.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: No MCP fee or per-call charge is documented by COROS. The public setup guide recommends paid ChatGPT Plus or Claude Pro, while noting platform policies vary.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: A COROS account and explicit OAuth authorization are required. Data must be synced to the COROS app/cloud. Account region determines routing. FIT retrieval has a shared allowance of 50 file/download-URL requests per connected platform user per fixed 24-hour window. AI client access and approval settings vary by platform.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: COROS controls account access, regional routing, MCP service, and documented FIT quota; the user authorizes the account connection; the AI platform controls its subscription, tool access, and approval settings.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. Official materials list query/read tools and tools that create, update, or schedule plans/workouts. No hosted tool annotations (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint) are published. 2. No server-enforced confirmation parameter or elicitation is documented. COROS docs advise confirmation in example prompts; public Skill directs client operators to obtain confirmation before plan creation. 3. OAuth scopes are openid, mcp.tools, offline_access. COROS states MCP reads only the authorized user's own activity data and uses existing coach/athlete visibility rules. DCR, PKCE S256, multiple grants, revocation, and TLS-bound access tokens appear in supplied metadata; token lifetime, admin switches, allowlists, and redirect approval are NOT FOUND. 4. Global URL routes by account region; standalone CN, EU, and US/other-region URLs are documented. Clients may control individual tool access/approval/blocking; no server read-only mode, toolset filter, or query-free mode is documented. 5. The server exposes health, menstrual-cycle, activity, profile, and device data. Docs describe account and permission boundaries but no field masking or PII exclusion. 6. FIT file and link calls share a 50-file per-user per-24-hour quota; per-tool date windows, record limits, page sizes, and caps are in the official tool guide. General rate limits and per-call cost are NOT FOUND. 7. Tool guide documents required fields, expected formats, constraints, and some corrections (reversed schedule date bounds are swapped). No general unknown-argument policy or server-side argument override behavior is documented. 8. Hosted logging, audit trails, and MCP telemetry are NOT FOUND. COROS's general privacy policy describes app/device processing and diagnostic logs, not MCP call logging specifics. 9. No feedback/rating/survey/report tool appears in the official 33-tool list. README directs users to GitHub Issues for feedback outside MCP. No tool-result upsell documented. 10. COROS publishes a separate login gateway Skill with workflow guidance; the Skill's behavioral instructions are not hosted server instructions. Tool descriptions advise reading details before edits and constrain editable record types; no hosted initialize instructions are published. 11. Hosted memory/state behavior is NOT FOUND. The separate Skill stores a short-lived local tool catalog and local auth state. 12. Standard flat documented tool list for the input host, with region-specific endpoints for routing. The separate local Skill is not a sub-server. 13. No raw API, arbitrary SQL, script execution, or general-purpose request tool is listed in the official tool guide.

E_aggregated.token_method: Hosted tool definitions and initialize instructions are not available verbatim. The public code is a client-side Skill helper, not the server implementation.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: COROS explicitly says plans/workouts cannot be deleted with AI; deletion must be done manually in the COROS app. Rescheduling/removing calendar workouts and exiting plans are also directed to the app. The support article says the MCP cannot query data belonging to another athlete or an athlete the user coaches. The support article describes GPS route, terrain/elevation-profile, split-trend, cycling power-curve, and FTP analysis as requiring raw FIT files or unavailable through basic query; it notes manual FIT export/upload as a workaround.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: COROS's tool guide recommends checking existing schedules before plan creation and reading details before edits; these are guidance in documentation. Tool guide constraints include 4–16-week plans, supported sports, editable-plan checks, and date windows, but server enforcement cannot be verified without hosted code. The separate Skill instructs clients to obtain user confirmation before plan creation; no server enforcement is documented.
F_documentation.governance_promises: COROS states: "Access is only granted through explicit user authorization." It says the MCP only queries the user's own activity data and applies existing coach/athlete visibility. It also says AI conversation retention is governed by the AI platform's policies. The COROS privacy policy covers health/training data processing in the app and wearables; it does not specify MCP-specific retention or logging.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: COROS describes MCP as a permission-based connection layer using existing account authentication and privacy controls. It says users choose whether to connect and which AI platform to authorize, and that the MCP itself is free.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: OAuth metadata verifies protected access and advertised scopes. Official docs describe user and data boundaries and tool-level limits, but hosted implementation is closed, so detailed enforcement, logging, and retention claims cannot be independently checked. Tool usage guidance and Skill confirmation instructions are not shown to be server-enforced.

contradictions: Manufact's listing reports 22 tools and includes analyzeActivityDetail, while the official changelog says analyzeActivityDetail was removed on 2026-10-23 and the current official guide names 33 tools. The catalogue appears stale.

Odel's listing says the publisher's server requires no sign-in, but its own text reports an OAuth sign-in at mcpus.coros.com; supplied endpoint evidence and OAuth metadata confirm protected OAuth access.
observations_for_research: The public repository distributes client-side Skill guidance and a login helper that dynamically discovers hosted tools, while the hosted server implementation remains closed.
COROS documents both read and write tools but leaves deletion, plan exit, and calendar rescheduling to the app.
Account authorization exposes the broad documented tool set through a single mcp.tools scope; tool-level allow, approval, and block controls are described as AI-platform features.
